rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings the clay to a complete human creation and an ordered human form.
rows.anchor: o balçığı tam bir beşer hilkatine, muntazam bir insan kıvamına koyup

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive 'My spirit' is an honorific genitive that ennobles the spirit by its attribution to God.
rows.anchor: burada رُّوحِى izâfeti bir izâfet-i teşrif

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about breathing into Adam is figurative, not a literal account of divine breathing.
rows.anchor: “nefh” tâbiri de bir temsildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God perfected matter's capacity and bestowed within it a spirit that is a divine command, as stated in 17:85.
rows.anchor: maddenin isti‘dâdını kemâle getirip bâtınına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels prostrate in obedience to God, submitting to the spirit-bearing human whom God thereby elevated above clay.
rows.anchor: o rûh bulunan insana inkıyad edin. İşte Allah, o balçıktan halk ettiği beşeri rûhuyla böyle yükseltmişti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Taha' is, God knows best, a set of alphabetic letters like the other disjointed openings.
rows.anchor: Tâ-hâ, Allâhu a‘lem, emsâli gibi hurûf-ı hecâdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes Taha as an oath by the Most Beautiful Names.
rows.anchor: esmâ-i hüsnâdan kasem olduğu söylenmiş

rows.speaker: bazı lügatlar
rows.claim: Some dictionaries give Taha the meaning 'O man!' or 'Hey, man!'.
rows.anchor: bazı lügatlarda “yâ recül, behey adam!” demek olduğu da rivayet edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading parses Taha as an imperative from وطأ/طا, addressing the Prophet to put his feet down or tread.
rows.anchor: emr-i hâzır, hâ zamir olarak “bas onu” yahut “çiğne onu” diye Resûlullah’a hitap olduğu zikredilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This imperative interpretation is linked to an instruction for the Prophet to put both feet on the ground during tahajjud instead of standing on one foot.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah, teheccüdünde bir ayak üzerinde durmakla iki ayağını da yere basması emrolunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer either to the Prophet's foot or to the earth, yielding 'put down your foot' or 'tread the earth'; Elmalılı calls the latter significant.
rows.anchor: Zamir kademe, yahut arza râci‘dir. Bu vechile “ayağını bas” yahut “arzı çiğne” demek de olabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth-treading interpretation would require the form to be written طاها rather than طه.
rows.anchor: buna göre طاها “tâ hâ” yazılması lâzım gelirdi

none: Translation only, followed by a bare lead-in to the next commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question can urge the disbelievers to look, ask whether they know, or consider the matter thoughtfully.
rows.anchor: Baksalar a. Veya haberleri yok mu, sorsalar a, veyahut şu re’y ü fikirde değiller mi?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of the heavens and earth as ratq is that they were sealed: no rain came down and no vegetation grew.
rows.anchor: retk idiler ikisi de deliksiz idi, yukarıdan yağmur yağmıyor, yerde ot bitmiyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading has the earth as an unbroken plain without mountains or valleys and the sky without sun, moon, or stars.
rows.anchor: Veyahut Arz dağsız deresiz yekpâre, eb‘âd-ı semâ da Şems ve Kamer’i, ecrâm ve kevâkibi yok yekpâre idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view says earth and celestial bodies were joined as one homogeneous matter, before diverse bodies existed.
rows.anchor: Arz ecrâm-ı semâviyeye bitişik, hepsi bir şeydi. O mütenevvî‘ecrâm ve ecsâm yok, hepsi mütemâsil bir madde idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that all shared an initial state of nonexistence, with no distinct external entities.
rows.anchor: veyahut hepsi ibtidâ ma‘dum olmakta müşterek idi, hâriçte mevcut ve mütemâyiz değil idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People could know these conditions through inference from observed events or through transmitted reports.
rows.anchor: Bunları da ahvâl-i meşhûdeden re’y ü istidlâl ile veya nakl ü sem‘ile bilirler veya bilebilirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God split and separated them: creation brought multiplicity from nonexistence and diversified an initial smoke-like matter into many celestial bodies.
rows.anchor: bir şey iken çoğaldılar. İbtidâ duman gibi bir madde iken müte‘addid ecrâm ve ecsâm oldular. Bir tabiatta kalamayıp

words: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water is the evident cause of life for all living things, including plants, animals, and humans.
rows.anchor: gerek nebât ve gerek hayvan, gerek insan zîhayat olan şeyin hayâtına suyu sebep kıldık

words: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ
rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some interpreters take the water here to mean semen.
rows.anchor: Bazıları burada sudan murad nutfe olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır

words: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers water in its ordinary sense, since the semen reading would restrict the scope to animals, while literal water includes plants too.
rows.anchor: Lâkin bu surette hayvânâttan bir kısmı hayy mefhûmundan tahsis olunmak îcab edecektir

words: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes that hydrogen, water's principal constituent, had come to be considered a basis of all elements, so the Quranic pointer embraces a wider truth.
rows.anchor: bütün anâsırın esası gibi mütalaa olunmaya başladığına nazaran

words: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ حَىٍّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Carbon's role in organic chemistry and air's relation to life do not contradict the verse; water is the clearest, most widely observable proof.
rows.anchor: zikr-i şey, mâ‘adâya münâfî olmadığı gibi bunlar umûm için su kadar bâriz ve meşhud da olmadığından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nature cannot explain itself: it cannot create the cosmos, separate earth from heaven, bring rain to dry air, or produce plants and diverse life from water by itself.
rows.anchor: Veya kuru havada yukarıdan yağmur yağar, kuru toprakta otlar biter miydi?

words: وَجَعَلْنَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ رَوَٰسِىَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God established firm mountains so earth's motion would not toss people about, giving them stable ground and making it habitable.
rows.anchor: sâkin olacak yer bulsunlar diye o Arz’da suya mukabil sulb oturaklı kıt‘alar, dağlar husûle getirdik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The open routes let people reach their destinations or find the path of guidance.
rows.anchor: ki hidâyeti bulabilsinler matlublarına doğru gidebilsinler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that the sky is protected from the assaults of devils, as 15:17 states.
rows.anchor: mantûkunca şeytanların taarruzundan mahfuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the sky is protected from corruption and disintegration until its appointed time, as 35:41 says.
rows.anchor: vakt-i ma‘lûmuna kadar fesad ve inhilâlden mahfuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People turn away from the many signs in the sky that point to God's power and oneness.
rows.anchor: Semâda Allah’ın kudret ü vahdâniyetine delâlet etmekte bulunan bunca delillerin delâletlerinden yüz çevirip geçiyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The celestial bodies move through their orbits; the verse does not say that a rotating sphere carries them around.
rows.anchor: Demek ki zannedildiği gibi onları felek döndürüyor değil, onlar felekte ve her biri bir felekte yüzüyorlar

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some take falak to mean a rotating thing and accordingly imagine it as a revolving physical sphere; Elmalılı says this reflects the science of their time.
rows.anchor: “Felek” devreden şey demek olduğuna göre bazıları feleği bir cism-i devvâr addetmişlerdir

rows.speaker: Dahhâk
rows.claim: Dahhak defines falak as the orbit or place where a celestial body revolves, a purely mathematical description.
rows.anchor: Dahhâk’ten rivayet olunduğu üzere “felek” nücûmun medârı, yani devrettiği mahal

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı notes that medar and the newer term mahrek designate a place of revolution or motion.
rows.anchor: “medar” kelimesi gibi “mahrek” demek de ıstılah olmuştur. Biri “devr”den ism-i mekân, biri de “hareket”ten ism-i mekândır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although only sun and moon are named, the plural yasbahun is noteworthy because it signals more than two subjects.
rows.anchor: haberde tesniye getirilmeyip de ikiden ziyadeyi ifade eden cemi‘sîgasıyla يَسْبَحُونَ buyurulması şâyân-ı dikkat görülmüştür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation supplies the omitted stars after sun and moon, with all referring collectively to the three.
rows.anchor: Birisi والشمس والقمر والنجوم takdîrinde olmasıdır ki Şems ü Kamer’in yanında nücûm hazf edilmiş, sonra da kül ve cem‘ile hepsine işaret olunmuş demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation treats sun and moon as names for a class of stars or celestial bodies.
rows.anchor: İkincisi bu karîne ile Şems ü Kamer’den cins-i nücûm kast edilmiş olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Within that generic reading, Elmalılı prefers taking sun and moon as encompassing all stars, some of which resemble moons, rather than leaving the other stars unmentioned.
rows.anchor: sâir yıldızların da kimisi Kamer mânasında olduğuna işâreten bu ikisini hepsinin cinsi gibi ahzetmek daha münâsibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that kull includes the previously mentioned earth along with sun and moon, so every body has its own orbit.
rows.anchor: “kül” ta‘mîmi Şems ü Kamer’le beraber mâkablinde zikri geçen Arz’ı dahi ihtivâ ederek hepsine işaret olmak da muhtemildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever the grammatical reading, Elmalılı says the verse overturns the old astronomy in which spheres were thought to move the sun and moon, and accords with bodies moving in space along their own axes or paths.
rows.anchor: Zira onlar Şems ü Kamer’i felek hareket ettiriyor diyorlardı. Burada ise her birinin birer felekte kendilerinin yüzdükleri haber veriliyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a scientific theory appears to conflict with the Quran, one should not bend the Quran to science; science should be reconciled with the Quran.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ı fenne uydurmaya çalışmamalı, fenni Kur’ân’a tevfik etmeye uğraşmalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordered, continuous motion of every celestial body, each on its own course and safely suspended, displays God's artistry, power, and oneness; unbelievers nevertheless turn away and attribute it elsewhere.
rows.anchor: hepsi muallakta, hepsi yolunda, hepsi nizâmında, hepsi mahfuz yüzüyorlar da yüzüyorlar. Bu ne bedî‘sanat, ne büyük kudret

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scientific teaching of the verse, alongside the earlier sign of earth's separation from heaven, is a divine sign of Muhammad's prophethood: Copernicus, Newton, or Laplace could discover the principle, but an unlettered Prophet's announcement of it before the world's sciences is miraculous evidence.
rows.anchor: bunu ümmî bir fıtratın bütün cihân-ı fenne karşı bir makām-ı tehaddîde haber verivermiş olması onun nübüvvetini meydana koyan

words: أَن لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders Jonah's prayer as affirming God's sole divinity, offering Him glorification, and confessing that he was among the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: Senden başka ilâh yok, Sana arz-ı tesbih ederim, ben doğrusu zâlimlerden oldum
